_validation_note: Audit of the v1 target (withdrawn). The PUCT-controls-posting chokepoint did not survive the controlling text: posting is a customer obligation to the interconnecting DSP or TSP under an intermediate agreement, study initiation is a DSP or TSP action directed by ERCOT protocols, and the commission's named roles are audit and enforcement. The AI or data-center scope was not established by primary text. No candidate survives all eight gates in this 21-day window, so this is an honest no-target. Earlier v1 target evidence is retained privately under .local/superseded.

dropped_mechanisms.name: Large-load financial security before study inclusion (v1 target, withdrawn on audit)
dropped_mechanisms.news_trigger: PUCT order adopting 16 TAC §25.194, Project 58481, Item 218, filed 9/18/2026
dropped_mechanisms.drop_reason: Audit failed two gates. (1) chokepoint_asymmetry: the v1 chokepoint named the Public Utility Commission of Texas as controlling whether a customer posts security. The adopted text does not support that. §25.194(d) makes the customer's execution and funding of an intermediate agreement with the interconnecting DSP or TSP a precondition to study inclusion, and that agreement names which entity accepts the security. §25.194(e)(1) makes the interconnecting DSP or TSP contact ERCOT within 60 days, as prescribed by ERCOT protocols. The commission's named roles in (d) and (e) are audit, staff verification and enforcement, and publishing adjusted values. No single institution holds the yes/no admission decision. (2) texas_consequence (AI/data-center scope): §25.194(b) applies to any large load of 75 MW or more at a single site and does not mention artificial intelligence or data centers. The only 'AI' term in the order is a commenter's company name. The data-center link comes from commenters and independent reporting, not from primary text. No fetched independent source corroborates the rule's adoption terms.
